paper.title: CoEvoSkills: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Co-Evolutionary Verification
paper.central_claim: CoEvoSkills lets an agent autonomously build multi-file skill packages by co-evolving a Skill Generator with an informationally isolated Surrogate Verifier (plus an opaque ground-truth pass/fail oracle); on SkillsBench it reaches 71.1% pass rate (+40.5pp over no-skill, +17.6pp over human-curated skills), outperforms five baselines, and the evolved skills transfer to six other LLMs (+35-44pp).

gap.author_gap: Human-authored skills are costly and unevenly useful (human-machine misalignment); tool-evolution methods handle single functions, not multi-file skill packages; EvoSkill needs ground-truth answers for diagnosis and held-out validation for selection.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete and sourced: SkillsBench shows degraded performance in some domains with human skills; neighbors (EvoSkill, SAGE, SkillRL, AutoSkill, AutoRefine, SEAgent) each assigned a stated limitation. However the claim of operating without ground-truth supervision is only partly true because an oracle pass/fail on the evaluation tests is consulted up to 5 times per task.
gap.lineage: Voyager-style tool/skill libraries -> self-evolving tool methods -> Anthropic skill-creator / SkillsBench -> EvoSkill (closest, uses GT diagnosis + validation selection) -> CoEvoSkills (isolated surrogate verifier + opaque oracle bit).
gap.closest_adjacent: EvoSkill (Alzubi et al.) is the closest and is characterized but not run as a baseline; SAGE/SkillRL are distinguished by training and single-file outputs.
gap.residue: Robust skill generation without test content or answers; multi-file packages.
gap.stakes: Performance gaps where human skills hurt (Natural Science) and authoring cost.
gap.method_response: Isolated surrogate verifier supplies dense diagnostics; oracle bit used to escalate tests.
gap.remaining_gap: Cross-task reuse of evolved skills, evaluation independent of the oracle used in selection, budget-matched comparison, open-world knowledge acquisition (authors' own future work).
unresolved: EvoSkill, SAGE, SkillRL, SkillsBench full texts are not in the pinned inputs; neighbor characterizations are taken from this paper only.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Both seats task; kept. Each skill is evolved per task with up to five pass/fail queries of that task's hidden tests, the best-oracle snapshot is kept, and the same tests score it. EVIDENCE rule 2: selection set ≠ held-out → at most task. Cross-model transfer is on the same tasks.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On 85 SkillsBench tasks, per-task skill packages evolved with an isolated surrogate verifier plus ≤5 opaque oracle bits on the same task raise a fresh Opus-4.6 agent's pass rate on those tasks (71.1% vs 30.6% no-skill, 5 runs). A single-run ablation attributes ~30pp to the verifier's dense diagnostics over oracle-bit-only evolution. Unseen-task benefit and the 'better than human skills' comparison are not established on like-for-like terms.
unresolved: Results on tasks not used for oracle-gated selection.
Reconciliation of ~88% oracle-pass (App. B), 75% (Fig. 2) and 71.1% deployed.

G.reason: Opus → sol 2 (son55 3). The bottleneck (single-pass multi-file skills unreliable; uneven human skills) is real and sourced (son55:E013, E014). But the gap is framed as working 'without ground-truth' and against EvoSkill's GT use (son55:E012), while the method itself consults each target task's hidden oracle up to 5 times and keeps the best snapshot (son55:E002, E021). That is a weaker held-out position than the held-out validation it criticises, so the residual gap over the nearest neighbour is not bounded. EvoSkill is not run. Not 1: the multi-file packaging problem is concrete.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Isolated verifier → dense diagnostics → repair, with escalation only on surrogate-pass/oracle-fail (son55:E022, sol:E02, E03). The prediction vs oracle-bit-only retries was tested (41.1% vs 71.1%; sol:E08). The surrogate–hidden-test alignment assumption is illustrated only by one case.

X.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Algorithm 1 (K, M, β, early exit, escalation trigger), the isolation rules and verbatim prompts make it reproducible (son55:E003, E024). Retention is per task, with no cross-task versioning (stated boundary; sol:E09).

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 3; kept, with an Opus shared correction to the reason. SkillsBench deterministic verifiers with an all-tests-pass criterion are credible (son55:E015). Opus adds that the reported counts do not reconcile: App. B implies ~88% oracle-pass over 85 evolution tasks (opus:O01, O03), Fig. 2 says 75% at round 5 (opus:O02), and the deployed headline is 71.1%. Whether 85 precedes the two exclusions is unstated (son55:E018). This is a reporting defect; the verifier itself is sound, so the rating stays 3.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. The w/o-surrogate arm (same oracle access, 5 iterations) is a fair internal control (41.1 vs 71.1; sol:E08). Baselines lack the oracle/iteration budget, human skills are generic vs per-task tuned (son55:E019, E020), ablations are single-run, and EvoSkill is not run.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. The hidden tests of each evaluated task select and stop its skill and also score it (son55:E002, E003; opus:O04). No unseen-task result exists. Partial credit only for opaque-bit limiting and fresh-environment re-execution; cross-model runs are on the same tasks.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 2; A2 ladder. Main methods: 5 runs ± std. Transfer: 3 runs. Ablations: single. No significance tests and no evolution-level variance.
